1280: They paid me in gold to haul locked crates, then paid me again to lose all curiosity about what was inside.
1281: The fancy stranger pointed at the heaviest crates, said 'those', and pressed gold into my hand for silence.
1282: Their locked boxes weighed like stone. They paid me in gold, so I stopped caring what makes a box that heavy.
1283: They watched me sweat under their crates from a folding chair, then paid me gold to forget I'd lifted them.
1284: A gold coin for every crate, they said, and a second gold coin never to ask what made them so heavy.
1285: The crates were locked, the locks were fancy, and the stranger paid in gold so I'd stop staring at them.
1286: They had me stack their locked crates just so, tipped in gold, and said the less I knew the happier I'd be.
1287: I've hauled cargo for twenty years. Nobody ever paid me gold to pretend the crates weren't clinking.
1288: The traveller wore silk and pointed at the biggest locked crate. Gold changed hands. I carried, I didn't ask.
1289: They handed me gold, then a locked crate, then more gold, then their finger to their lips. I understood.
1290: I've lifted a lot of crates. Only these ones came with gold and a firm, smiling request that I not open them.
1291: They ordered me around like a duke, but the gold was real, so I hauled their locked boxes and kept quiet.
1292: One crate, they said, was very fragile and very heavy and very much none of my business. Then, gold.
1293: They tipped me gold to load fast and gold again to swear I never saw the locks on those crates.
1294: The stranger inspected my muscles, chose me for the heavy locked crates, and paid in gold for my silence.
1295: I asked what was inside just once. They laughed, added another gold coin, and that was my answer.
1296: They stood in polished boots while I hauled their locked crates, then paid gold and vanished from the dock.
1297: The crates clinked, the stranger glittered, and the gold was enough that I decided the clinking was nothing.
1298: They wanted the crates loaded by hand, not by crane, and paid gold so I wouldn't ask why they were so precious.
1299: I lifted their locked crates, my back complained, their gold apologized, and I asked no questions at all.
1300: They demanded I shove the biggest ship aside so theirs could pass first, tapping a foot the whole time.
1301: They insisted the whole harbor should hold still until I towed the biggest ship somewhere less inconvenient.
1302: They pointed at the biggest ship and told me to nudge it aside, as if the whole port existed for their schedule.
1303: I've towed liners twice their size, but this one wanted them all moved so their boat could go first.
1304: The stranger checked a jeweled watch and huffed that a mere giant ship was blocking someone as important as them.
1305: They boarded barking orders and informed me their schedule outranked a ship roughly the size of a small town.
1306: Move the big one, they said, waving a gloved hand, as though ships parted for anyone who looked expensive enough.
1307: They complained the harbor was slow, then blamed the slowness entirely on one ship, which I was to remove at once.
1308: They stamped a polished boot and demanded the whole port rearrange itself so their vessel wouldn't have to wait.
1309: I told them the big ship couldn't just move. They offered gold and demanded I move it anyway, immediately.
1310: The stranger declared the largest ship an inconvenience and insisted I tow it aside for their grand departure.
1311: They stood at the rail like a monarch, sighing loudly, waiting for me to clear a giant ship from their way.
1312: Everyone else can wait, they announced, so long as the biggest ship is dragged aside for them first.
1313: The impatient stranger tapped their watch at me until I promised to shove the largest vessel out of their lane.
1314: They boarded in a swirl of fine coat, glanced at the harbor's biggest ship, and asked me to make it stop existing there.
1315: The grandest passenger I've towed decided a colossal ship was simply in their way and told me to fix that.
1316: They gestured at the largest ship as if it were a chair I'd left out, and told me to please move it aside.
1317: They explained that their minutes were far too valuable to spend behind a ship, so I should simply move the ship.
1318: The stranger's boat was small, their demands enormous: clear the biggest ship, and be quick about it.
1319: They ordered the harbor cleared for their grand exit and drummed their fingers until I towed the big ship aside.
